name: TX-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Huge GOP fundraising and outside-spending advantage over a barely funded Democrat
Open seat removes incumbent advantage but not the district's lean
Prediction markets price a Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: TX-08 leans Republican by 13 points, and Steinmann has raised $2.4 million with $1.7 million in outside support while Jones has raised under $30,000. Markets price the Republican at about 94%, so the seat stays likely Republican despite the open-seat status.
model.watch: A late Democratic-funded intervention or an unexpected GOP primary fallout could narrow the margin, but nothing in the evidence suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-08 is a solidly Republican Houston-area seat with a 13-point Republican partisan lean, and incumbent Morgan Luttrell is retiring. Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised about $2.4 million and benefited from roughly $1.7 million in outside support. Democrat Laura Jones has raised under $30,000 with no reported outside spending.

Prediction markets give the Republican about a 94% chance of holding the seat, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The open-seat dynamic removes some incumbent cushion, but the district's fundamentals and the spending gap point to a Republican hold in the mid-teens.
